options.text: A single beam strong enough to hold any weight
A set of connected parts that work together to carry loads
Any object taller than a person
A pile of building materials kept on a site

items.explanation: A structural system is a set of connected parts that work together to carry loads and hold a shape. The job of staying up is shared among the parts.

items.stem: Which component carries weight straight down to the foundation?
items.explanation: Columns are upright parts that carry weight straight down to the foundation. They are mainly in compression.

items.stem: A horizontal part that spans across open space and carries weight to the columns is called a
items.explanation: A beam is a horizontal part that spans across open space and carries weight to the columns. Floors and bridge decks rest on beams.

items.stem: The steady weight of a building's own beams, walls, and floors is its
items.explanation: The dead load is the constant weight of the structure itself. It does not change from day to day.

items.stem: Which of these is the best example of a live load?

options.text: The weight of the steel columns
A crowd of people gathering on a balcony
The roof panels bolted in place

items.explanation: A live load is a changing weight that comes and goes. A crowd of people is a live load, while the columns, foundation, and roof are dead load.

items.stem: Which force stretches or pulls a material apart?
items.explanation: Tension is a force that stretches or pulls a material apart. A bridge cable holding up the deck is in tension.

items.stem: A column under a heavy roof is being squeezed together. This force is
items.explanation: Compression is a force that squeezes or pushes a material together. A column under a load is in compression.

items.stem: Wind makes a tall tower twist, turning the top relative to the base. This twisting force is
items.explanation: Torsion is a twisting force that turns one end of a material relative to the other. Wind can twist a tall structure with torsion.

items.stem: Why are triangles used so often in bridges and trusses?

options.text: They are always the cheapest shape
They hold their shape under load instead of folding
They are the only shape that floats
They make a structure lighter than any other shape

items.explanation: A triangle holds its shape under load because its angles cannot change without bending a side. That makes triangles the most stable shape for structures.

items.stem: In 1940 the Tacoma Narrows Bridge twisted apart in the wind. This failure happened because the bridge could not resist

options.text: the weight of its own paint
torsion, the twisting force from the wind
the dead load of its towers

items.explanation: The bridge failed because it could not resist torsion, the twisting force created by the wind. Engineers now design bridges to handle that force.
